newsitem.title: UK: T-bond quiet in London, focus on data and rates.
newsitem.headline: T-bond quiet in London, focus on data and rates.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries in London were quiet on Thursday and analysts said there was little incentive to trade ahead of U.S. data later in the session and next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
With the market divided about whether the Federal Reserve will raise rates or not at the FOMC on May 20, few players were prepared to enter the market, they said.
"It's snooze city," said Nick Benton, Treasuries trader at BankAmerica in London. "The market is just sitting there waiting."
At 1023 GMT the long bond was at 96-20 to yield 6.89 percent. This compared with 96-18 in Tokyo and 96-23 in New York.
Two-year T-notes were at 100-07, from 100-08 in Tokyo and New York, while five-year notes were at 100-11, down slightly from 100-13 at the Tokyo and New York closes.

"The debate is, is the economy growing at a record pace or are there any signs of slowing? Some people have interpreted (Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's) comments as meaning that if there are signs of slowing he will hold off until July or perhaps later in the year," Benton said.
In light of the uncertainty about rates he said the U.S. April industrial production and capacity utilisation data due at 1315 GMT would take on new importance.
Production is forecast to rise 0.2 percent versus 0.9 percent rise previously, while capacity utilisation is expected to come in at 84.1 percent, unchanged from March.
"If they came in significantly above the market's expectations, the market would take it poorly," he said.
Other data to be released this session include April consumer prices at 1230 GMT, and the Philadelphia Fed survey, some of the first data for May at 1400 GMT.
Weekly jobless claims and April real earnings are also due at 1230 GMT and 1400 GMT respectively.

Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi International in London, said the overall tone of the data should be supportive for the market, but this could be offset by the weakness of the dollar and the continued unwinding of yen carry trades.

"On the face of it today's data should argue for upside but the dollar is a major focus for the market at the moment and continued dollar weakness could be the preoccupation of the market over and beyond the support of domestic fundamentals," Chester said.
June T-bond futures were at 100-01, down four ticks in automated trade, while LIFFE June T-bond futures were trading at 110-01 up 5/32 on the day.
